concept: A comeback told in the order it happened. The hero puts the half-time scoreline in muted grey and the result in white, so the eye reads the swing from 'down' to 'champions', with 10 titles and 3 in a row in the fact row. Slide 2 freezes the one minute that flipped the final: a giant 59' for the VAR red card, with Bhat's equaliser landing a minute later. Slide 3 is a four-line match timeline (45+1', 59', 60', 88') so fans can replay the night at a glance, then asks whether the red card decided it. Football green, type and pitch graphics only: no player photos, no federation logos.
caption:
1-0 down at half-time. Champions by full-time.

India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final in Dhaka tonight to win a record 10th title. It is the first time India have won three editions in a row.

Why it turned: Pakistan led through Alamgir Ghazi's curling finish in first-half stoppage time. In the 59th minute Junaid Shah was sent off after a VAR review for a challenge on Brison Fernandes. One minute later Suhail Ahmad Bhat equalised.

Against 10 men India kept pushing. Sandip Mandi headed in Abdul Rabeeh's corner in the 88th minute.

Pakistan were playing their first SAFF final. Did the red card decide it or would India have come back anyway? Tell us below.
